Mina — draft below (internal/legal-approved language). I've included operational notes after the paragraph. Please review and let me know if you want anything softened for the customer-facing doc.

---
Customer-facing assurance (legal-approved):
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided content for improving or training our public models, nor do we perform model re-training using customer data. For hosted and Dedicated deployments, we commit that customer data will not be incorporated into model training datasets or used to update model weights; derivative-model artifacts for product telemetry or quality analysis are produced only in aggregated, de-identified form and are governed by contractual restrictions. For Private (VPC or on-prem) deployments, the customer retains full control of data and configuration; Redwood does not access or train on data in private deployments unless explicitly arranged and contractually agreed."

Operational summary (key points):
- KV cache: Ephemeral by default. Per-request KV entries are held in memory and evicted based on TTL. Default TTL is session-scoped (60 minutes); can be configured for Dedicated customers. KV cache is not persisted to long-term storage in Hosted or Dedicated unless a customer enables a snapshot/ingest flow.
- Logs/telemetry: Access logs, request traces, and usage telemetry are stored per the customer's retention tier. Standard hosted retention is 90 days for detailed request bodies; metadata and aggregated metrics retained up to 24 months by default. We offer shorter retention and custom retention via contract amendments.
- Snapshots/backups: Regular model-serving snapshots (checkpoints) do not contain customer request payloads. Any system backups that contain transient request data are on a rolling retention and can be purged on demand; deletion requires coordination with our infra team and will be tracked via a ticket.
- Deletion & erase requests: For Hosted/Dedicated, we provide an erase workflow: submit a request via support, infra runs targeted deletion (cache purge, log redact, snapshot purge if applicable), and we issue a deletion report. SLA target: 10 business days for standard erase; expedited options available under enterprise SLA.
- Evidence: We can provide a SOC2 Type II control narrative excerpt and a signed retention exhibit showing agreed retention windows.

Operational exceptions / notes:
- Edge/Private deployments: Deletion paths vary (customer-managed storage; Redwood may not have direct control in on-prem installs). For VPC deployments where we have limited access, deletion is coordinated and may rely on customer-run scripts or a joint runbook.
- Backups: Immutable backup retention windows are governed by infra policies; deletions of immutable backups are subject to restore windows and may require ticketed processes.

Attachments to include for FinHealth: SOC2 excerpt + retention exhibit (I attached drafts).

Priyom
Legal & Privacy (on-call)

Alex — thanks again for the patience. See the canonical statement and ops summary below; I attached a SOC2 excerpt and a retention exhibit that match the wording. In short: Redwood does not train or re-train models using customer-provided content in Hosted or Dedicated deployments, and we provide an operational deletion flow for logs, KV cache, and any snapshots that contain request material.

Quoted for your vendor review (feel free to attach):
"Redwood Inference does not use customer-provided content to train or update model weights. Customer data will not be added to training corpora or used to produce derivative model weights. Aggregated and de-identified telemetry may be used to monitor service health and improve product performance, subject to contractual restrictions and with no linkage to customer-identifiable content"

Key operational points (summary):
- KV cache is ephemeral by default (session-scoped TTL ~60 min) and not persisted to long-term stores unless explicitly configured.
- Request-level logs (including payloads) are retained per the contracted retention tier; standard hosted retention is 90 days for full request bodies. Shorter retention can be contractually defined.
- Backups/snapshots do not contain training data; any transient request data in backups is on a rolling retention and removable via our deletion workflow.
- Erase requests: standard SLA 10 business days; expedited 3 business days with an enterprise SLA addendum. We provide a deletion report when complete.

Attachments: SOC2-TypeII-summary.pdf (control narrative excerpt), data-retention-sla-exhibit.pdf (shows configurable retention tiers and erase SLA).
